proposed_from.topic: Exact-hit information deficiency and minimax design for ranking exact treatment saturations. Fix K≥2, equal cluster size n, distinct interior rational exact-count policies pi_k=m_k/n, iid clusters with unrestricted binary within-cluster interference schedules, and exact-slice welfare targets. Compare fixed-count two-stage complete randomization with iid nominal labels followed by unit-Bernoulli assignment. Let B_kl=Pr(Bin(n,pi_l)=m_k) and q=Bp. Prove the target-tangent lower experiment and local minimax regret bound by holding nontarget-count laws fixed, match it with assignment-calibrated cross-label exact-hit estimation, derive the primitive joint CLT, consistent studentization and rank set, characterize sharp CR/Bernoulli equality and strict-loss conditions, solve the complete two-policy allocation map, and give a certified general-K Gaussian-risk/outer-simplex computation. Use the four-node pi={1/4,1/2} witness and Egger et al.'s Kenya saturation design as consumer; distinguish Han–Owusu–Shin, Joo's downstream Gaussian selection result, Chan et al., and Loomba–Eckles. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact nuisance deletion and an independent target-bit submodel derive pooled hit rates q=Bp. Recalculation gives B=[[27/64,1/4],[27/128,3/8]], optimal first-label share 0.39383577843, local regret penalty 1.26189430297, and sample-size penalty 1.59237723186 relative to optimized exact-count assignment. Raw pooling is not pointwise efficient when within-slice assignment means differ; calibration over the observed assignment fixes this without changing the target. Checks covered zero hits, boundary shares, unequal variances, separated versus tied means, informative nontarget schedules, shrinking variances, common-parameter games, and 280840 two-count menus; no verified collision appeared. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a certified general-K Gaussian minimax selector on the full contrast space with partial ties and covariance perturbations, then transfer its risk uniformly to the primitive calibrated cluster experiment. EARLY KILL TEST: At n=4 and pi={1/4,1/2}, verify tau²/q information for both the independent tied target-bit submodel and the legal assignment-heterogeneous means (4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5), and match the two-point Gaussian lower bound to pooled regret; failure stops the kernel. seed_details.referee_objection: Equality holds exactly when every active label assigns probability one to target counts, which is immediate for endpoint labels.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; the endpoint case is retained only as a sanity reduction, not a proposal angle.

proposed_from.literature_map: Han, Owusu, and Shin (2026, arXiv:2606.18590) is the same-target anchor. Its Appendix B identifies exact-count complete-randomization welfare from Bernoulli data using \(\mathbf 1\{L=k\}\) and the within-label Radon--Nikodym weight; it neither pools a realization of count \(m_k\) from a different nominal label nor derives the target tangent experiment. Its design theorem minimizes a regret envelope, and its local ranking result is restricted to threshold rules under rank-one variation. Loomba and Eckles (2026, arXiv:2609.02756), Proposition 1, constructs the unique minimum-\(L^2\) transport weight by projecting the full inverse-probability weight onto a Fourier subspace. That projection motivates score projection here, but its target is Bernoulli-policy transport under structured interference rather than an unrestricted exact slice. Joo (2025, arXiv:2509.03796) characterizes a one-shot Gaussian minimax-regret selector by least-favorable-prior duality on \([-B,B]^K\) and proves covariance continuity on a compact positive-definite class. The full translation-quotiented contrast game and admissible covariance-boundary transfer needed for exact-hit design are outside those stated compact domains. Kato, Imaizumi, Ishihara, and Kitagawa (2026, arXiv:2506.24007) take finite sequential Gaussian games through expanding boxes and give certified tail calculations for adaptive best-arm sampling. This supplies a closer certification template than Joo alone, but the sequential controller is not the static one-shot Gaussian selector and its allocation is not constrained by \(q=Bp\). Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, Theorems 3.1--4.2) provide the limit-experiment lower-bound and plug-in-decision architecture; the present first changed step is to derive the exact-hit information experiment from the primitive schedule law rather than assume a reward CLT. Stoye (2009, Journal of Econometrics, Section 2.2 and Proposition 2) supplies the finite-sample least-favorable-prior certificate and the binary-outcome reduction; it does not contain several coupled exact-hit cells or optimal saturation-label design. Baird, Bohren, McIntosh, and Özler (2018, Review of Economics and Statistics) optimize randomized saturation designs for power and document the precision cost of learning saturation-specific effects. Their criterion is not simple regret and has no binomial cross-label hit map. Jiang, Imai, and Malani (2023, Biometrics) stack two-stage causal means and derive joint covariance and Wald procedures. Their fixed strategy cells motivate the covariance calculation, while calibrated hit scores replace the disjoint cells. Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm (2024, Review of Economic Studies) invert simultaneous pairwise tests to obtain rank confidence sets from a joint approximation. Their theorem begins after the joint approximation is available and does not address exact-hit sparsity or calibration. Chan, Nakamura-Sakai, and Forastiere (2023, ACIC poster) already combine nominal Bernoulli labels for hypothetical-allocation spillover estimands. This nonarchival source prevents any claim that cross-label weighting alone is novel; the new objects are exact-count welfare, saturated nuisance deletion, calibrated information, and mechanism-level regret loss. Egger, Haushofer, Miguel, Niehaus, and Walker (2022, Econometrica, Section 2.3 and Appendix A) randomized 68 saturation groups between one-third and two-thirds village treatment intensities. It is the concrete design consumer, subject to the explicit isolation and equal-size scope conditions.
